label: Bonus Class 2
title: Sounds Arabic Doesn't Have: P, V and the Buzz
titleAr: أصوات ليست في العربية: P و V والطنين
bigIdea: Many English sounds come in twins: same mouth, but one buzzes in the throat and one only whispers. Arabic has b and f, but not their twins p and v, so we train them on purpose.
bigIdeaAr: كثير من أصوات الإنجليزية تأتي توائم: الفم نفسه، لكن أحدهما يطنّ في الحلق والآخر يهمس فقط. في العربية الباء والفاء، لكن ليس فيها توأماهما p و v، لذلك ندرّبهما عن قصد.
builtOn: Lessons 5-8: numbers 11-20, colors, I like... / I don't like... (food: pizza, apple, peas, fish)
Phonics groups 3-4 (Lessons 5 and 7): g, o, c, k, ck, e, u, r
Bonus Class 1: letters vs sounds, consonants vs vowels, the Vowel Elevator and the vowel friends Lazy A, Quick E and Smiley I

objectives.en: I can feel if a sound buzzes (voiced) or whispers (voiceless) with my hand on my throat.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أشعر بيدي على حلقي إن كان الصوت يطنّ (مجهوراً) أو يهمس (مهموساً).

objectives.en: I can say p with a puff of air and b with a buzz: pin / bin, pig / big.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أنطق p بنفخة هواء و b بطنين: pin / bin و pig / big.

objectives.en: I can say v with my top teeth on my bottom lip and a buzz: fan / van.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أنطق v بوضع أسناني العليا على شفتي السفلى مع طنين: fan / van.

objectives.en: I can hear and say short o and short u apart (hot / hut) and say a soft English r.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أميّز وأنطق o القصيرة و u القصيرة (hot / hut) وأن أنطق r الإنجليزية الناعمة.

keyTerms.meaning: A sound where the voice box buzzes: b, d, g, v, z.
A sound with no buzz, only air: p, t, k, f, s.
The part of your throat that buzzes. Inside it are two tiny curtains called the vocal folds.
Two sounds made in the same place in the mouth; one buzzes, one whispers: p/b, t/d, k/g, f/v, s/z.
The little burst of air after p, t and k at the start of a word: pin, ten, cat.

linguisticsCorner.title: The buzz box in your throat

facts.en: In your throat there is a voice box with two tiny curtains called the vocal folds. When they shake together very fast (hundreds of times every second!) you hear a buzz. That buzz is your voice.
facts.ar: في حلقك صندوق صوت فيه ستارتان صغيرتان اسمهما الحبلان الصوتيان. عندما تهتزّان بسرعة كبيرة جداً (مئات المرات في الثانية!) تسمع طنيناً، وهذا الطنين هو صوتك.

facts.en: Some sounds use the buzz (voiced: b, d, g, v, z, m, n and all vowels). Some sounds are only air (voiceless: p, t, k, f, s). Put your hand on your throat to feel the difference.
facts.ar: بعض الأصوات تستعمل الطنين (المجهورة: b و d و g و v و z و m و n وكل الحركات)، وبعضها هواء فقط (المهموسة: p و t و k و f و s). ضع يدك على حلقك لتشعر بالفرق.

facts.en: Sound twins: p and b are made in exactly the same place (both lips). The big difference is the buzz: b buzzes, p does not. The same is true for t/d, k/g, f/v and s/z. (English p, t and k also have a puff: see the next fact.)
facts.ar: توائم الأصوات: p و b تُصنعان في المكان نفسه تماماً (الشفتان معاً)، والفرق الأكبر هو الطنين: b تطنّ و p لا تطنّ. وكذلك t/d و k/g و f/v و s/z. (ومع p و t و k في الإنجليزية نفخة هواء أيضاً، كما في المعلومة التالية.)

facts.en: At the start of a word, English p, t and k come with a little puff of air. A tissue in front of your mouth flutters for pin but stays almost still for bin. After s the puff almost disappears: spin has a much smaller puff than pin. English listeners notice this puff even more than the buzz, so a clear puff is the best way to make pin sound different from bin.
facts.ar: في أول الكلمة تخرج مع p و t و k في الإنجليزية نفخة هواء صغيرة. المنديل أمام فمك يرفرف مع pin ويكاد لا يتحرك مع bin. وبعد s تكاد النفخة تختفي: نفخة spin أصغر بكثير من نفخة pin. والأذن الإنجليزية تنتبه لهذه النفخة أكثر من انتباهها للطنين، لذلك فالنفخة الواضحة هي أفضل طريقة لتجعل pin مختلفة عن bin.

facts.en: English r is a soft sound: the tongue tip lifts and pulls back but does not touch the top of the mouth. Arabic ر taps or rolls (the tongue tip hits the bump just behind the top teeth). In American English, as in our lessons, the r at the end of car is said: /kɑːr/. In standard British English it is usually not said (British /kɑː/). Both are correct.
facts.ar: صوت r الإنجليزي ناعم: يرتفع طرف اللسان ويرجع إلى الخلف لكنه لا يلمس سقف الفم. أما الراء العربية فيضرب فيها طرف اللسان اللثةَ خلف الأسنان العليا مرة أو أكثر. وفي الإنجليزية الأمريكية، كما في دروسنا، تُنطق r في آخر كلمة car: /kɑːr/، أما في الإنجليزية البريطانية القياسية فلا تُنطق غالباً (البريطانية /kɑː/)، وكلاهما صحيح.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic ب is the buzzing twin. Arabic has no whispering twin, so p often turns into b (pizza becomes 'bizza'). Persian and Urdu added a new letter for it: پ (ب with three dots underneath).
arabicBridge.pointAr: الباء العربية هي التوأم الذي يطنّ، ولا يوجد في العربية التوأم الهامس، لذلك يتحوّل p غالباً إلى ب (pizza تصبح 'بيتزا'). الفارسية والأردية أضافتا له حرفاً جديداً: پ (باء بثلاث نقاط من تحتها).

arabicBridge.point: Arabic ف is the same as English f (whisper). Arabic has no buzzing twin v, so v often turns into f (seven becomes 'sefen'). Some Arabic writers use ڤ (ف with three dots on top) for v, as in ڤيتامين.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الفاء العربية مثل f الإنجليزية تماماً (همس). ولا يوجد في العربية التوأم الذي يطنّ v، لذلك تتحوّل v غالباً إلى ف (seven تصبح 'سِفِن'). بعض الكتّاب العرب يستعملون ڤ (فاء بثلاث نقاط من فوقها) لصوت v كما في ڤيتامين.

arabicBridge.arabic: ج المصرية / ق في لهجات الخليج
arabicBridge.point: Good news: g is easy for us. In Cairo and much of Egypt ج is said as g (جمل = gamal), and in the Gulf ق is often said as g (قال = gaal). Use that sound.
arabicBridge.pointAr: خبر جميل: صوت g سهل علينا. في القاهرة ومعظم مصر تُنطق الجيم g (جمل = gamal)، وفي الخليج تُنطق القاف غالباً g (قال = gaal). استعمل هذا الصوت نفسه.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic ر taps or rolls on the roof of the mouth. In English r the tongue tip touches nothing: tip up and pulled back, lips a little round, no rolling.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الراء العربية تضرب سقف الفم أو تتدحرج. أما في r الإنجليزية فطرف اللسان لا يلمس شيئاً: يرتفع ويرجع إلى الخلف، والشفتان مستديرتان قليلاً، بلا تدحرج.

arabicBridge.point: Both letters are often read as damma, but neither is damma. o in hot: mouth wide open, an open 'ah' with lips not round, /ɑː/ (British English: short, with lips a little round, /ɒ/). u in hut: a short relaxed 'uh', lips NOT round. Damma is nearer to the u in put.
arabicBridge.pointAr: كثيراً ما نقرأ الحرفين ضمةً، لكنّ أيّاً منهما ليس ضمة. o في hot: الفم مفتوح جيداً، وهي 'آ' مفتوحة بلا استدارة للشفتين /ɑː/ (وفي النطق البريطاني قصيرة والشفتان مستديرتان قليلاً /ɒ/). u في hut: صوت قصير مرتاح 'أَه' بلا استدارة للشفتين. الضمة أقرب إلى u في كلمة put.

commonErrors.why: Arabic has no p, so the brain picks the nearest Arabic sound, ب. Use the tissue test: p needs a puff.
Over-correction: after practicing p, some children put p everywhere. Hand on throat: b buzzes.
Arabic has f but no v. Keep the teeth on the lip and switch on the buzz.
Arabic ر taps the roof of the mouth. The tip of English r touches nothing: Puppy R, not Motorbike R.

commonErrors.wrong: hot for hut, cop for cup
commonErrors.why: Both letters are often read as damma. Round O opens the jaw wide (round lips in British English); Grumpy U is short and relaxed, lips not round.

commonErrors.wrong: soon for sun, boos for bus
commonErrors.why: Reading u as a long Arabic و (oo). Short u in a CVC word is a quick 'uh'.

teacher: A paper tissue (or a thin strip of paper)
Sound twin cards: p/b, t/d, k/g, f/v, s/z
Character cards: Puffy P, Bouncy B, Very Vibrating V, Puppy R, Round O and Grumpy U (plus Lazy A, Quick E, Smiley I from Bonus Class 1)
Minimal-pair word cards: pin/bin, pig/big, pat/bat, pet/bet, cap/cab, fan/van, hot/hut, cot/cut, dog/dug, not/nut
student: A paper tissue or a thin strip of paper
A small mirror (or the camera self-view)
Six paper cards with big letters: p, b, f, v, o, u

stages.name: Warm-up: Vowel Friends Wake-up
stages.purpose: Recall the Bonus Class 1 vowel friends and the elevator, and get mouths moving before the new sounds.
teacherSays: Hello, Sound Scientists! Who remembers our vowel friends? Show me Lazy A! (yawn) Quick E! (quick point) Smiley I! (tiny pinch)
Ride the Vowel Elevator: a... e... i! Down again: i... e... a!
Quick! Which friend is in cat? In ten? In big?
Today we meet some sounds that Arabic doesn't have. Are you ready to be brave with your mouth?
teacherSaysAr: مَن يتذكّر أصدقاء الحركات؟ أروني A الكسولة و E السريع و I المبتسمة!
اليوم نتعرّف على أصوات ليست في العربية. هل أنتم مستعدّون؟
studentsDo: Do each vowel friend's gesture and sound.
Ride the elevator with a hand on the chin.
Name the friend in cat, ten, big, red, pin.
tips: Keep it to 3-4 minutes; it is a switch-on, not a test.
Have the tissues ready on the desk now so stage 4 does not stop for searching.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: Buzz or Whisper?
stages.method: Guided discovery with touch (hand on throat) and the sound-twins pattern
stages.purpose: Discover the voice box and that English consonants come in twins that differ only in the buzz.
teacherSays: Put your hand on your throat, here. Say zzz like a bee. Do you feel it shaking? That is your voice box buzzing!
Now say sss like a snake. Any buzz? No! Only air. sss is a whisper sound.
Inside your voice box there are two tiny curtains. For buzz sounds they shake very fast. For whisper sounds they stay open and the air just goes out.
Now look: zzz and sss. Same mouth, same teeth, same tongue. Only the buzz is different. They are twins!
Let's find more twins. ffff... vvvv. Hand on throat! Which one buzzes?
Our biggest twins today: p and b. Lips together for both. b buzzes, p whispers and puffs.
teacherSaysAr: ضع يدك على حلقك وقل zzz مثل النحلة. هل تشعر بالاهتزاز؟ هذا صندوق صوتك يطنّ!
zzz و sss توأمان: الفم نفسه، والفرق فقط في الطنين.
studentsDo: Hand on throat: say zzz / sss, vvv / fff, bbb (b-b-b) / ppp (p-p-p) and feel buzz or no buzz.
Show a thumbs-up for buzz and a flat hand for whisper.
Say each twin pair while watching the mirror: the mouth looks the same for both.
Sort sounds on the slide into the Buzz box or the Whisper box.

exercise.instructions: Hand on your throat. Say the sound. Buzz or whisper? Show thumbs-up (buzz) or flat hand (whisper).
exercise.instructionsAr: ضع يدك على حلقك وانطق الصوت. طنين أم همس؟ ارفع إبهامك (طنين) أو افتح يدك (همس).

tips: Long sounds (zzz, vvv, fff, sss) are the easiest to feel. Start with them, then try b and p by repeating them: b-b-b, p-p-p.
Say consonants pure: 'b', not 'buh'. 'buh' adds a vowel and every vowel buzzes, so p would seem to buzz too.
If a child cannot feel the buzz, ask them to put both hands over their ears and say zzz: the buzz is loud inside the head.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: The Missing Twins
stages.method: Contrastive analysis with a twins chart (English vs Arabic)
stages.purpose: Show exactly why p and v are hard (Arabic has only one twin of each pair) and that other twins are already easy.
teacherSays: Look at our twins chart. t and d: Arabic has ت and د. Easy! s and z: Arabic has س and ز. Easy!
k and g: Arabic has ك. And g? In Egyptian Arabic, ج says g: gamal. In the Gulf, قال is often gaal. So g is easy for you too!
b and p: Arabic has ب... but where is p? Missing! f and v: Arabic has ف... but where is v? Missing!
These are the missing twins. Your mouth has never needed them in Arabic, so we will train them today.
Fun fact: Persian and Urdu borrowed Arabic letters and added three dots to make پ for p. Some Arabic writers use ڤ for v, like in ڤيتامين!
teacherSaysAr: في العربية التاء والدال، والسين والزاي، والكاف وصوت g في بعض اللهجات. لكن أين توأم الباء؟ وأين توأم الفاء؟ مفقودان!
الفارسية والأردية أضافتا ثلاث نقاط فصنعتا پ لصوت p.
studentsDo: Read the Arabic letter for each twin on the chart: ت/د, س/ز, ك/g, ب/?, ف/?.
Point to the two empty boxes (the missing twins p and v).
Say pizza the Arabic way and the English way; spot the difference.
tips: Be positive: Arabic has many sounds English does not have (ع، ح، خ، ض، ق). Every language picks its own sounds.
Some children already say p and v in loanwords (pizza, video) from cartoons or school. Praise them and use them as models.

stages.name: Puffy P and Bouncy B: The Tissue Test
stages.nameAr: P النفّاخ و B القافزة: اختبار المنديل
stages.method: Multisensory articulation (tissue, hand in front of mouth, throat) + character mnemonics + minimal pairs
stages.purpose: Produce a clear aspirated p and a buzzing b, then hear the difference in minimal pairs.
teacherSays: Meet Puffy P! He blows out birthday candles: p! p! p! Hold your tissue in front of your lips. Say pin. Did the tissue jump?
Meet Bouncy B! She has a buzz in her throat and no big puff: b! b! Hold the tissue. Say bin. The tissue stays almost still.
Put your other hand on your throat. pin: no buzz, big puff. bin: buzz, small puff.
Now I say a word. Show me p or b! pig... big... pat... bat...
Let's say pizza with Puffy P: p-p-pizza! Your tissue should dance!
teacherSaysAr: P النفّاخ يطفئ شموع عيد الميلاد: p! امسك المنديل أمام شفتيك وقل pin. هل تحرّك المنديل؟
B القافزة فيها طنين في الحلق ولا تنفخ كثيراً.
studentsDo: Hold a tissue (or paper strip) 3 cm from the lips and say p-p-p, then b-b-b.
Say the pairs pin/bin, pig/big, pat/bat, pet/bet with tissue and throat check.
Listening: show the p or b card for each word the teacher says.
Say pizza, pink and peas with a strong puff, then apple (p in the middle: lips close, no buzz, only a small puff).

exercise.instructions: Listen to the word. Show the p card or the b card.
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع للكلمة وارفع بطاقة p أو بطاقة b.

tips: The puff is strongest at the start of a word (pin, pig). At the end of a word (cap) the lips close and the puff is small, so check end sounds by ear, not with the tissue. A clue: the vowel is a little longer before b (cab) than before p (cap).
If a child says b for p, ask them to whisper the word first (a whisper has no buzz), then say it again a little louder keeping the puff.
Watch for over-correction: if big becomes pig, go back to the throat: 'Where is Bouncy B's buzz?'

stages.name: Very Vibrating V and Fluffy F
stages.nameAr: V المهتزّة جداً و F الناعمة
stages.purpose: Produce v (top teeth on bottom lip plus buzz) and keep it different from f in known words like seven, eleven, twelve and five.
teacherSays: Look in the mirror. Put your top teeth gently on your bottom lip. Blow: fff. That is Fluffy F, like ف in Arabic. Easy!
Keep your teeth there. Now switch on the buzz: vvv. Your lip tickles! That is Very Vibrating V.
Hand on throat: fff (no buzz), vvv (buzz). Twins again!
Numbers have v inside! sev-en, e-lev-en, twelve, five. Five starts with f and ends with v: f... v. Feel it!
Chant with me: 'Five vans, very fast! Seven vans, very fast!'
teacherSaysAr: ضع أسنانك العليا بلطف على شفتك السفلى وانفخ: fff مثل الفاء. ثم شغّل الطنين: vvv. شفتك تدغدغك!
في الأرقام صوت v: seven و eleven و twelve و five.
studentsDo: Mirror check: teeth on lip for both f and v (not both lips like b).
Hold vvv for 3 seconds and feel the lip tickle.
Say fan/van, five, seven, eleven, twelve, very with the mirror.
Say the chant and clap on every v.

exercise.instructions: Listen. Do you hear Fluffy F or Very Vibrating V? Show the f card or the v card.
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع: هل تسمع F الناعمة أم V المهتزّة؟ ارفع بطاقة f أو v.

tips: Some children replace v with b or w. Use the mirror: v needs teeth on the lip; b and w use both lips.
The letters f and v come formally in later phonics lessons (f in Lesson 9); here they are practiced as sounds, so the words are simple and mostly known (numbers, fish, fine).

stages.name: Round O, Grumpy U and Puppy R
stages.nameAr: O المستدير و U المتذمّر و R الجرو
stages.method: Character mnemonics + Vowel Elevator + minimal pairs + gesture contrast for r
stages.purpose: Separate short o (hot) from short u (hut) and replace the rolled Arabic ر with a soft English r.
teacherSays: Two new vowel friends! Meet Round O. He is surprised and opens his mouth wide: o! hot, dog, top. Make an O with your fingers around your mouth.
Meet Grumpy U. He is a bit grumpy and says a short, relaxed 'uh': u! up, cup, sun, run. Lips relaxed, not round. Arms crossed!
Mirror check: hot... jaw wide open. hut... short and relaxed. hot, hut! dog, dug!
Careful: in Arabic we read both like damma, but damma pushes the lips forward. Grumpy U never pushes his lips.
Now r. Arabic ر is a Motorbike R: rrrr, the tongue taps and rolls. English r is a Puppy R: a soft little growl, the tongue tip pulls back and touches nothing. rrr... red, run, rat.
Tip: start with your lips a little round, like a tiny o, then say red.
teacherSaysAr: O المستدير متفاجئ: فمه مفتوح جيداً: hot و dog. U المتذمّر يقول 'أَه' قصيرة والشفتان مرتاحتان: up و cup و sun.
الراء العربية مثل الدرّاجة النارية: تتدحرج. أما r الإنجليزية فمثل زمجرة جرو صغير: اللسان لا يلمس شيئاً.
studentsDo: Copy Round O (finger circle) and Grumpy U (crossed arms) with each sound.
Mirror pairs: hot/hut, cot/cut, dog/dug, not/nut, lock/luck.
Listening: show the o card or the u card.
Say Motorbike R (Arabic) then Puppy R (English): red, run, rat, rug, rock. Check: does your tongue touch? It should not.

exercise.instructions: Listen to the word. Show Round O (finger circle) or Grumpy U (crossed arms).
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع للكلمة. اصنع دائرة بأصابعك لـ O المستدير أو اعقد ذراعيك لـ U المتذمّر.

tips: Keep the o simple: in American English, as in our lessons, the o in hot is an open 'ah' /ɑː/ with no rounding; in British English it is short with slightly rounded lips (British /ɒ/). Either is fine as long as it is clearly different from Grumpy U. The mirror check contrasts a wide-open jaw (hot) with a short, relaxed 'uh' (hut); with the British o you can also point to the slightly round lips.
On the Vowel Elevator, Round O lives on the ground floor next to Lazy A (jaw open), with round lips in British English; Grumpy U lives in the middle, relaxed.
For r, 'don't roll it' is hard for a child to follow. Let them feel the difference instead: tap ر, then pull the tongue tip back for r.

stages.name: Sound Twins Challenge: Be the Teacher
stages.nameAr: تحدّي توائم الأصوات: كن أنت المعلّم
stages.purpose: Use all the new sounds in speaking and listening, with children testing each other.
teacherSays: Game time! I give one child a secret word card in the private chat. You say the word. The others show the card: p or b, f or v, o or u.
If the group shows the right card, the speaker AND the group get a point. Clear sounds win!
Now our tongue twisters. Slowly, then fast!
'Puffy P puts pink peas in a pot.' / 'Bouncy B has a big blue bag.' / 'Seven vans, very fast!' / 'Grumpy U runs up in the sun.'
teacherSaysAr: سأرسل لك كلمة سرّية في الدردشة الخاصة. قلها، والباقون يرفعون البطاقة الصحيحة.
إذا رفع الجميع البطاقة الصحيحة يحصل المتكلّم والمجموعة على نقطة!
studentsDo: Take turns saying a secret minimal-pair word; the others show the card.
Give feedback to a friend: 'More puff!' or 'More buzz!'
Say each tongue twister slowly, then fast, with the tissue for the p twister.
Choose your favorite twister and say it alone.

exercise.instructions: Listen to your friend. Which word did you hear? Type it in the chat or show the card.
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع لصديقك. أي كلمة سمعت؟ اكتبها في الدردشة أو ارفع البطاقة.

tips: If the group shows the wrong card, it is usually the speaker's sound, not the listeners' ears: coach the speaker kindly and try again.
Teams private chat works well for secret words; with young children a parent can help read it.
Make sure every child is both speaker and listener at least twice.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Goodbye
stages.purpose: Check each child can hear the new contrasts alone and finish with a fact to share at home.
teacherSays: Exit ticket! I say five words. Write the letter for the sound you hear: p or b, f or v, o or u.
Did you know? Every language chooses its own sounds. English has p and v but no ع or ح. Arabic has ع and ح but no p or v. Now your mouth can do both. You are becoming a sound scientist!
Your mission at home: do the tissue test with your family. Can they say pizza with a puff?
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ كل لغة تختار أصواتها. في الإنجليزية p و v وليس فيها ع ولا ح، وفي العربية ع وح وليس فيها p ولا v. والآن فمك يستطيع الاثنين!
مهمتك في البيت: جرّب اختبار المنديل مع عائلتك.
studentsDo: Write the letter for 5 words.
Say goodbye with Puffy P: 'Bye-bye, p-p-pizza!'
tips: Note who scored under 4/5 for extra minimal-pair practice in Lessons 9-11 warm-ups (Lesson 9 teaches b and f, a perfect moment to revisit p and v).

exitTicket.instructions: Listen. Write the letter you hear: p or b (first sound), f or v (first sound), o or u (middle sound).
exitTicket.instructionsAr: استمع واكتب الحرف الذي تسمعه: p أو b (الصوت الأول)، f أو v (الصوت الأول)، o أو u (الصوت الأوسط).

homework.en: Tissue Test at Home: show your family Puffy P and Bouncy B with a tissue and the buzz with a hand on the throat. Then say five words with p (pizza, pink, pen, pig, apple) and three numbers with v (five, seven, eleven).
homework.ar: اختبار المنديل في البيت: أرِ عائلتك P النفّاخ و B القافزة بالمنديل، والطنين باليد على الحلق. ثم قل خمس كلمات فيها p (pizza و pink و pen و pig و apple) وثلاثة أرقام فيها v (five و seven و eleven).
tasks: Do the tissue test with pin / bin and pig / big for a family member.
Say the four tongue twisters to someone at home.
Draw Round O and Grumpy U and write two words under each (hot, dog / sun, cup).

support: Work on one contrast only (p/b) and leave v and o/u for the next warm-ups.
Let the child show the gesture or card instead of writing.
Use only word-initial sounds (pin/bin), where the puff is easiest to see.
challenge: Find the twins in the words: tap/dab, cap/cab, fan/van. Which sounds change?
Try the spin test: does the tissue move more for pin or for spin? (pin: after s the puff almost disappears.)
Make a new tongue twister with v (very, van, vet, seven).

successCriteria: Correctly sorts at least 8 of 10 sounds as buzz or whisper.
Shows the right card for at least 8 of 10 p/b listening items.
Says pin and bin so that the tissue clearly moves for pin only.
Says hot and hut with two clearly different vowels, and red with an unrolled r.
watchFor: b said as p after practice (over-correction)
rolled Arabic r in red, run
u read as long oo (sun -> soon)

teacherNotes: This class is about the sound system, not new vocabulary: the words are known lesson words (pizza, peas, pink, apple, red, fish, numbers) or simple CVC words.
The letters b and f are formally taught in Lesson 9 and v in Level 2. Here they are practiced as sounds; children already know ب and ف, so the sounds themselves are familiar.
Do not over-correct accent. The goal is a clear contrast (pin is not bin), not a native accent.
Reuse 'More puff!', 'More buzz!' and the Round O / Grumpy U gestures as quick corrections in later lessons.
Bonus Class 3 builds on this: blending sounds into words and segmenting words into sounds.

deck.title: Wake up, vowel friends! Show me the gesture

deck.instructions: Listen. Which vowel friend is in the word?
deck.instructionsAr: استمع: أي صديق من أصدقاء الحركات في الكلمة؟

deck.title: Hand on your throat!
deck.text: Your voice box has two tiny curtains. For buzz sounds they shake very fast. For whisper sounds they stay open.
bullets: zzz like a bee: your throat shakes
sss like a snake: only air, no buzz
Thumbs-up for buzz, flat hand for whisper
deck.ar: في صندوق صوتك ستارتان صغيرتان: تهتزّان مع أصوات الطنين، وتبقيان مفتوحتين مع الهمس.

deck.title: Twins: same mouth, but one buzzes
rows: top teeth on the bottom lip

deck.noteAr: انطق كل توأمين ويدك على حلقك: الفرق فقط في الطنين!

deck.instructions: Hand on your throat. Say the sound. Buzz or whisper?
deck.instructionsAr: ضع يدك على حلقك وانطق الصوت: طنين أم همس؟

deck.title: Which twins does Arabic have?
rows: ك، وصوت g: الجيم المصرية والقاف الخليجية
deck.note: Arabic has b and f, but not their twins p and v. And Arabic has sounds that English doesn't have!
deck.noteAr: في العربية ب و ف، لكن ليس فيها توأماهما p و v. وفي العربية أيضاً أصوات ليست في الإنجليزية: ع وح وخ!

deck.title: Letters with three dots for the missing twins

cards.head: v in some Arabic writing

deck.ribbon: Sound lab · Puffy P, Bouncy B
deck.title: The tissue test: hold a tissue in front of your lips

cards.head: Puffy P
cards.sub: A big puff! The tissue jumps. No buzz.
cards.ar: P النفّاخ: نفخة قوية بلا طنين

cards.head: Bouncy B
cards.sub: A buzz in your throat. The tissue stays almost still.
cards.ar: B القافزة: طنين في الحلق بلا نفخة كبيرة

deck.title: Tissue up! Say each pair

lines.en: apple: lips close, a small puff

deck.tip: The tissue jumps for p. Your throat buzzes for b.

deck.instructions: Listen to the word. Show the p card or the b card.
deck.instructionsAr: استمع للكلمة وارفع بطاقة p أو بطاقة b.

deck.ribbon: Sound lab · Fluffy F, Very V
deck.title: Mirror check: top teeth on your bottom lip

cards.head: Fluffy F
cards.sub: Blow: fff. Just like Arabic ف. No buzz.
cards.ar: F الناعمة: مثل الفاء، بلا طنين

cards.head: Very Vibrating V
cards.sub: Same teeth, switch on the buzz: vvv. Your lip tickles!
cards.ar: V المهتزّة جداً: الأسنان نفسها مع الطنين

deck.title: Clap on every v!

lines.en: five: f at the start, v at the end

deck.tip: Teeth on your lip for v. Both lips for b!

deck.instructions: Listen. Fluffy F or Very Vibrating V? Show the f card or the v card.
deck.instructionsAr: استمع: هل تسمع F الناعمة أم V المهتزّة؟ ارفع بطاقة f أو v.

cards.head: Round O
cards.sub: Surprised! Jaw wide open. Make an O with your fingers.
cards.ar: O المستدير: متفاجئ وفمه مفتوح جيداً

cards.head: Grumpy U
cards.sub: Short, relaxed 'uh'. Lips NOT round. Arms crossed!

deck.title: Mirror pairs: swap o and u, make a new word

deck.instructions: Listen. Finger circle for Round O, crossed arms for Grumpy U.
deck.instructionsAr: استمع: دائرة بأصابعك لـ O المستدير، وذراعان معقودتان لـ U المتذمّر.

deck.title: Two kinds of r: does your tongue touch?

cards.head: Motorbike R (Arabic)
cards.sub: rrrr! The tongue tip taps or rolls.
cards.ar: الراء العربية: يضرب طرف اللسان أو يتدحرج

cards.head: Puppy R (English)
cards.sub: A soft little growl. Tip back, touching nothing, lips a little round.
cards.ar: R الجرو: زمجرة ناعمة، واللسان لا يلمس شيئاً

deck.instructions: Listen to your friend. Which word did you hear? Show the card.
deck.instructionsAr: استمع لصديقك: أي كلمة سمعت؟ ارفع البطاقة.

deck.title: Slowly first, then fast!

lines.en: Puffy P puts pink peas in a pot.
lines.ar: P النفّاخ يضع بازلاء وردية في قِدر.

lines.en: Bouncy B has a big blue bag.
lines.ar: B القافزة معها حقيبة زرقاء كبيرة.

lines.en: Grumpy U runs up in the sun.
lines.ar: U المتذمّر يركض صاعداً تحت الشمس.

deck.tip: Tissue up for the p twister! Clear sounds win, not speed.

deck.text: Every language chooses its own sounds. English has p and v but no ع or ح. Arabic has ع and ح but no p or v. Now your mouth can do both!
deck.ar: كل لغة تختار أصواتها. في الإنجليزية p و v وليس فيها ع ولا ح، وفي العربية ع وح وليس فيها p ولا v. والآن فمك يستطيع الاثنين!

missions.title: Puff or Buzz?
missions.intro: Listen. Do you hear Puffy P or Bouncy B at the start?
missions.introAr: استمع: هل تسمع P النفّاخ أم B القافزة في أول الكلمة؟

missions.title: Round O or Grumpy U?

missions.introAr: استمع للكلمة وضع o أو u في الفراغ.

missions.title: Buzz or Whisper?
missions.intro: Tap a sound to hear it. Hand on your throat! Then tap its box.
missions.introAr: اضغط الصوت لتسمعه، وضع يدك على حلقك، ثم اختر صندوقه.

items.q: p and b are both made with your two lips.
items.qAr: يُنطق p و b كلاهما بالشفتين.

items.q: Arabic has a letter for the p sound.
items.why: Arabic has ب (b) but no p. Persian and Urdu use پ.

items.q: For f and v, your top teeth touch your bottom lip.
items.qAr: مع f و v تلمس أسنانك العليا شفتك السفلى.

items.q: The u in sun is a long oo, like soon.
items.qAr: u في sun صوت طويل مثل soon.
items.why: Grumpy U is a short, relaxed 'uh': sun, not soon.

items.q: English r rolls, like Arabic ر.
items.qAr: r الإنجليزية تتدحرج مثل الراء العربية.
items.why: English r is a soft Puppy R: the tongue touches nothing.
